title: Provisioning Note: The Top-Up Reserve Carried on Long Keyturn Trip Booking Reservations
content:
Where included miles are topped up on a Keyturn Trip Booking whose reserved period runs for 60 days or more, a top-up reserve is added to the miles the top-up must cover, and the reserve is the wider of the two figures where the vehicle has already been driven hard.

**Where the reserved period runs for 60 days or more and the reservation's odometer readings have booked more than 3000 miles**, the top-up reserve is 800 miles.

**Where the reserved period runs for 60 days or more and those readings have booked 3000 miles or fewer**, the top-up reserve is 400 miles.

**In every other case** the top-up reserve is the standard one.

### Reading the two conditions

The days of the reserved period are counted from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted. Sixty days is reached rather than passed, so a reserved period of exactly 60 days meets that limb and one of 59 days does not.

The odometer readings counted here are the records the reservation's mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics, the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked.

The miles the readings have booked are the driven miles taken off the reservation's allowance by those readings. The threshold is passed rather than reached: readings booking exactly 3000 miles fall in the lower band and give a reserve of 400 miles, while readings booking 3001 miles give 800 miles.

| Reserved period | Miles the readings have booked | Top-up reserve |
|---|---|---|
| 60 days or more | More than 3000 | 800 miles |
| 60 days or more | 3000 or fewer | 400 miles |
| Fewer than 60 days | Any | The standard one |

*Hypothetical.* A reservation of 84 reserved days whose readings have booked 4100 miles carries a top-up reserve of 800 miles. The same reservation with 2200 miles booked carries 400 miles. A reservation of 40 reserved days whose readings have booked 4100 miles carries the standard reserve, because the reserved period is short of 60 days.
